note: A forked workflow plugin (synapse, AllHailSeizure/Synapse -> rudi193-cmd/synapse) was audited against Nestor's rules and a fleet-wide skill survey. Most of synapse's discipline core duplicates willow-mcp's live skills (debugging exact-name, review, tdd, brainstorming, worktree) fleet-wide, but Nestor's seat.md walls Nestor off from willow-mcp, so those are unreachable inside a Nestor dev session and standalone skills here are not redundant for Nestor. The cream of the crop was landed into .claude/skills/ as four Nestor-native skills (verification, testing, debugging, autonomous-work-boundaries), re-landed from synapse's method rather than copied.

decisions.question: Landing the best synapse dev skills into Nestor -- copy synapse's SKILL.md files, or re-land them native?
decisions.commitment: Re-land, not copy. Each of the four skills under .claude/skills/ was authored in Nestor's voice against Nestor's own commands (bash scripts/ci-lint.sh, python -m pytest -q), docs (seat.md, agent-guide.md), the decision store, and the propose-not-confirm refusal -- keeping synapse's method (hypothesis-first debugging, test-the-forbidden-act, intent/execution boundary) while sharing no file with synapse. .claude/skills/README.md credits synapse as the source idea and records the diff that informed selection.
decisions.why: Copying synapse's files verbatim would create a vendored pair -- synapse's original and Nestor's copy -- that this repo's Shape 12 / section 16 discipline (and quick-stupids' re-land-don't-copy rule) exists to refuse: two copies, one of which a later session fixes while the other rots. Re-landing leaves no shared file to drift, only a shared idea, credited. It also let the willow-mcp versions be harvested for disciplines synapse lacked (search prior context first, surgical fix, commit-message format, never mock the thing under test) instead of importing either wholesale.

decisions.question: Which synapse skills are landed now, and which are held?
decisions.commitment: Landed four: verification, testing, debugging, autonomous-work-boundaries -- the ones that map 1:1 onto Nestor's load-bearing disciplines (don't overclaim, prove a guard can fail, fix surgically with evidence, know the propose/confirm line) and need the least adaptation. Held: finishing-branches, bug-capture, goal-oriented-development, worktree-cleanup -- they shell gh (this environment is GitHub-MCP only) and/or auto-open PRs (Nestor's standing rule is no PR unless asked), so they must be adapted before landing. Skipped: asset-churn-audit (game-asset tool, Nestor ships no binary art). thinking / writing-plans / executing-plans / code-review are a possible next tranche.
decisions.why: The cream is the set that is both highest-value for Nestor and least in conflict with its rules. Landing the gh/auto-PR skills unadapted would import a clash the audit already flagged; landing an N/A asset tool would be noise. Naming the held and skipped sets in the same commit keeps the selection honest -- what was left out and why, not a silent subset.
